notes: This contract pins Umbra's opt-in, non-installable IEEE 1516.1-2025 object-instance Request Attribute Value Update development slice to the exact C++ request and Provide Attribute Value Update callback declarations exported by the Requirements Lab. It verifies only the official signatures, declared exception sets, adapter symbols, and real Catch2 selectors. The slice validates the requester's currently known instance/class boundary, groups currently owned requested attributes by owner, does not invoke a requester for attributes it owns, skips unowned attributes, propagates the user tag, and rechecks a queued provider before callback delivery. A focused production-filesystem case also proves the provider's private service-report append precedes callback user code for the explicit object-instance path. It only solicits the callback; it does not implement automatic provision or a subsequent value-update response. The sibling object-class overload has its own traceability contract. Regional request overloads, timestamped/retraction behavior, DDM, update-rate reduction, ownership transfer, FOM sharing-policy enforcement, save/restore, remote transport, packaging, catalog evidence, and conformance remain outside this slice.
